findings.title: verifier_entrypoint_is_safe_and_always_scores
findings.evidence:
Authority and identity: I read the actual frozen XLSX with openpyxl: rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx, Quality Checks sheet row 22 (quality number 21), says test.sh must launch safely, gate on liveness, run gates before scored with score.py after each, and write a reward on every code path. I also read Internal Quality Checks row 22 and Deterministic Checks rows 7, 33 and 36. The matching frozen skill quality-checks.md:92-94 requires unprivileged launch, symlink escape refusal, early zero reward and ensured exits; staged-task-contract.md:98-111 describes the ordered contract. Current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md requires distinguishing source, scripted product observations and full verifier evidence. T below denotes .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task. The manifest input is a6a5219e9c5aa5e19c2b30acb01ca3a1719938a02ea09674cd18e08987bf43a9. Actual file hashes match manifest entries for test.sh, score.py, restart_mcp.py, workbook, skill and all three cited references.

Positive source findings and error-path audit: T/tests/test.sh:14-23 defines complete plain-zero outputs and nonempty-file fallback; lines 60-61 write zero and install the EXIT cleanup before checking judge variables, server.js or submission symlinks. Missing judge/model (63-66), missing entry (68-70), rejected symlink (72-83), copy/permission/setup errors under set -e (90-95), startup readiness failure (115-125), restart-helper/prompt preparation error (127-201), gates-suite nonzero/timeout (203-215), and scored-suite nonzero/timeout (224-226) therefore already have zero reward files. Lines 72-83 reject links outside the allowed node_modules tree; 104-111 launch through setsid, env -i and UID/GID 65534. Readiness probes occur before RewardKit. Lines 212-227 clear old scored output, run gates, call score.py, preserve the detailed zero on true gate failure, overwrite with plain zero for scorer errors, then run scored and score.py again. A scored-suite failure retains the gate-only aggregate, whose reward is still zero; it need not imply missing output. score.py:35-60 explicitly gives zero when scored data is absent; validates finite numeric dimensions (13-20); exceptions return 2 (86-91), which the caller handles. No shell exec replaces the trapped process; find -exec at line 86 is not that prohibited construct. Successful scoring preserves its nonempty files through ensure_reward. Bash syntax validation of this exact frozen test.sh returned 0; both shared Python tools parsed successfully. These are source/parser observations, not an end-to-end verifier run.

Credible inherited defect 1, unsafe restart success: T/tests/test.sh:152-159 sends TERM and polls the old process group 50 times, but after exhausting that loop it continues with no failure or KILL. Lines 160-169 launch a replacement and overwrite app.pid. Lines 170-183 decide success solely from probe_ready; there is no kill -0 check of the new PID, no assurance the old group died, and no attribution of the responding listener. probe_ready at 130-145 accepts any HTTP response from port 3000, including HTTPError. Thus the existing still-running listener can supply the response while the replacement has failed with EADDRINUSE. T/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:restart translates helper exit 0 into the explicit claim 'the server was relaunched on the same database and answers HTTP'. The functional prompt relies on that completion at T/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:23 and 363-369, and criterion cw_process_restart_durability at judge.toml:347-351 awards actual process-restart survival. A false helper success can therefore award survival without process replacement. This is a direct control-flow counterexample, not a regex heuristic or a claim that the current golden earned a wrong score.

Credible inherited defect 2, unbounded cleanup: T/tests/test.sh:33-40 performs 'kill -- -"$APP_PID"' and then 'wait "$APP_PID"' before ensure_reward, without a deadline or forced termination. A launched child that remains alive after TERM can stall this EXIT trap indefinitely. The prewritten zero or already computed reward generally remains present: this finding DOES NOT establish that a reward is absent. Its demonstrated source consequence is unbounded verifier termination and failure to reach the final ensure_reward call; the eventual host-timeout treatment is unmeasured. After restart overwrites app.pid with a dead replacement, cleanup also loses its reference to a surviving old group.

Inherited-template constraint: byte comparisons found the frozen task and frozen template test.sh identical, SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa; score.py also identical (13de2b3885967e22aa13ded3bf33c354e3e741e85be871612c04e996eef5c04e) and restart_mcp.py identical (03c1426f00e451f4d86b7547761715328c63cdf299f5f812f46c9fa3b44979b5). These defects are inherited harness conflicts, not unauthorized task-specific drift. The shared-template preservation rule prevents silently fixing them in this review.

Executed evidence and its limits: golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json and actual-restart.json record one successful ordinary restart, PID 16 to 335, 5.645670579979196 seconds; the earlier 070305 run records 16 to 336. Both name the canonical MCP hash above and helper-template hash 0db23e8c7c8d70c7e934c4d13ccbb2326a4da2cb47f1b2ba1967009d829be3b7, which I independently derived from the frozen heredoc. The 070504 saved-record/read-write facts after restart passed. Its executed drivers/launch_workflow.py:38 launches the server separately; 59-64 extract only the helper; 69-72 call MCP and additionally await the original server exit; 85-91 implement separate Python cleanup. It does NOT execute the full canonical test.sh, its EXIT trap, RewardKit gates/scored suites, or score.py. No resistant-process, replacement-failure or canonical error-path run is present in those observations. The normal successful restart does not refute either source counterexample. The full configured judge, Oracle score and behavior under the listed adverse paths remain unmeasured. No new Docker/provider run was performed.
findings.impact: Source-derived, not executed in this audit. False pass: a Node server holds its saved library in memory, accepts independent-browser saves/readbacks and registers process.on('SIGTERM', () => {}); its existing listener survives the helper's five-second poll. The replacement cannot bind port 3000, but the old listener answers the helper's HTTP probe. MCP reports restart completion, the original memory still serves the records and later saves, and the restart-survival criterion can pass without a process restart. Conforming alternative at risk of false failure: a correct SQLite-backed app implements an eight-second graceful SIGTERM shutdown, which the public integration contract does not prohibit. The same helper can claim completion from that old listener after five seconds while its replacement fails to bind; the old process subsequently exits and downstream browser checks lose the otherwise conforming service. Cleanup witness: an otherwise functional server with a retained TERM handler can keep the EXIT trap at the unbounded wait, even though its initialized reward files still exist.
findings.fix: Escalate the inherited conflict to the shared harness owner rather than changing task-controlled settings. In a newly authorized canonical candidate, bound process-group shutdown, verify old-group death and replacement PID liveness before accepting HTTP readiness, and ensure reward preservation plus original exit status survive bounded cleanup. Measure the exact canonical entrypoint against ordinary and TERM-resistant apps, children, a replacement that exits, suite/scorer failures and both zero/nonzero preexisting rewards; retain the current normal-restart evidence only by matching hashes.

Functional/cw_stale_save_server_refusal and cw_stale_save_draft_recovery (judge:361-372; S23:375-380) own independent server-refusal and real-editor retention/recovery evidence in both cycles. Functional/cw_harmless_scope_words and cw_unsupported_execution_refused (judge:137-148; S08:214-228) cover the harmless control and FIVE separate bounded family probes, with an independent last-good fallback. Functional/cw_snippet_network_boundary (judge:130-134; S07:204-208 plus supplied routing recipe:27-95) uses matching working transport controls and separate fetch/Image attempts, counts delivery and checks visible refusal/recovery. 18. security.md:11 says save/load store source as text and "Source entered into the editor is never evaluated on the server." Exact text roundtrip maps to Constraints and cw_saved_record_fidelity, but the no-server-execution promise has no owner or distinguishing observation: see G1.
19. instruction.md:7 and ui.md:3,5,7,9 require three useful panes, narrow-screen access, editor monospace/line numbers/syntax colouring, requested controls, light/dark workspace themes, labelled controls, visible keyboard focus, pointer-free navigation and legibility. Functional/cw_editor_monospace, cw_editor_line_numbers, cw_editor_syntax_colouring (judge:312-330; S19:346-348) cover editor mechanics. cw_theme_actual_switch and cw_theme_work_preserved (judge:403-414; S34:395) exercise both theme transitions while preserving state; authored preview recolouring is optional. Visual/visual_typography, visual_color_and_contrast, visual_spacing_and_layout, visual_hierarchy_and_scanability, visual_overall_craft and visual_responsive_consistency (visual/judge:24-104; visual/prompt:17-22,35-37) cover desktop craft, both offered themes and cross-viewport composition while Polish owns mobile operability. No exact colour, layout, control label, shortcut hint or editor package is required.
20. instruction.md:1, overview.md:7 and policy.md:3 require no accounts/sign-in. Render opens without sign-in; both gates and all scored in-dimension prerequisites use the public shared library. No authentication criterion is imposed. policy.md:5 freedoms over labels, indentation, routes and request fields are respected by UI-purpose matching and discovery of actual request formats. instruction.md:9 / security.md:9 / policy.md:7 permit app external assets; no same-origin demand is added.
21. Runtime/deliverable requirements in instruction.md:5,9 and integration.md:3-11 are only partly assured by the grading profile. test.sh:68 checks server.js presence, :97-111 starts Node on PORT 3000 with DB_PATH and NODE_PATH, and :48 probes health/root; Constraints checks health and the local server-backed save/read. S22 grades restart behavior. The frozen template itself mandates Node/Express/better-sqlite3, SQLite/DB_PATH, one process and no external backend (R/projects/webdev-task-template/environment/instructions/integration.md). Exact Express/SQLite use, single process count, absence of a proxy to an external backend, honouring a non-default DB_PATH under the normal writable-/app path, and 0.0.0.0 rather than loopback binding are not established by matching browser data. Task-specific source/build-file delivery, /app/public/index.html placement, absence of startup installation and independence from runtime /assets or /instructions likewise have no independent browser criterion. Some are exercised indirectly by successful startup in the separate image, but startup is not proof of all these literal assurances. This is a declared runtime/profile assurance limit, not evidence of a bad reference implementation or a new requirement to inspect source. React/TypeScript/Vite are expressly optional (integration.md:3), so there is NO missing mandatory frontend-stack check. Keep canonical harness/settings unchanged; resolve exact-stack assurance centrally rather than silently adding browser-source inspection or calling the constraint gate proof of SQLite.

Credible product coverage defects:
G1 (P1, task-specific security promise, source-confirmed / counterexample runtime NOT EXERCISED): security.md:11 promises server non-evaluation. No criterion covers it. Constraints:25-29 and S21/S22/S23/S24 only compare stored text and records; Functional prompt:7 forbids implementation/database inspection and limits evidence to product actions. A plausible otherwise-correct implementation evaluates each saved/loaded .js string in a bounded server VM for validation/metadata, suppresses VM console/errors and then stores/returns the original bytes. It produces every prescribed preview/library outcome while directly violating this promise. Browser roundtrip is not evidence of non-evaluation. Add a bounded save/load execution-boundary outcome with a supported observable negative witness and explicit limits, or resolve the absolute implementation assurance through approved profile policy; do not simply award it from storage fidelity.
G2 (P1, ungraded invalid creation branch, source-confirmed / mutant runtime NOT EXERCISED): behaviour.md:25 distinguishes new drafts from updates and :27 applies nonempty/unique titles to saved snippets generally. Yet S24:387-388 probes ONLY Source's CURRENT revision and observed Save-update format; all new records in S01/S21/S22/S23/S24, Constraints and Polish have valid unique titles. A product that trims on create but omits empty/duplicate checks in its create UI/endpoint, while correctly validating all updates, meets every written scenario. Its users can create empty or duplicate records. Extend the existing title outcomes with ordinary New/Save invalid-create probes and corresponding valid-create controls, checking the complete library unchanged, without assuming POST/PUT routes or schemas.
G3 (P2, missing HTML asynchronous error-coordinate branches, source-confirmed / mutant runtime NOT EXERCISED): behaviour.md:15 explicitly says HTML line numbers count from the complete document, followed by "The same applies to errors thrown later by a timer and to unhandled Promise rejections." S11:267-277 uses only synchronous undefinedFunctionCall at document line 6. S12:285-288 uses delayed-error.js line 2; S13:296-299 uses rejected-promise.js line 2. A compiler that applies HTML's pre-script offset only in its synchronous catch, leaving timer/rejection handlers to report inline-script-relative lines, passes all four scenarios but misreports the required asynchronous HTML lines. Add bounded complete-HTML timer and rejection fixtures with markup before their script, reusing existing error/line/rollback owners and setup observations.
G4 (P2, missing duration observations for non-success outcomes, source-confirmed / mutant runtime NOT EXERCISED): behaviour.md:19 says "Show how long each run took." cw_console_duration at functional/judge.toml:274 narrows this to "The completed Run shows a measured duration" and S16:326 observes only console.log('history-first') success. S03/S04/S09-S13/S36 require reasons, errors, rollback/recovery, but never require an elapsed duration for their stopped, failed or timed-out run. Polish:68 accepts status, new output OR an empty state, so it cannot fill this gap. An implementation displaying elapsed time only on successful completion, hiding it on error/Stop/timeout, passes those prescribed observations. Reuse the already-performed lifecycle scenarios to record their displayed elapsed durations under the duration owner; do not repeat expensive scenarios.

Conforming-alternative challenge: traced a vanilla-JS frontend (the named React/TypeScript/Vite tools are optional), a server-rendered library without a separate JSON list route, arbitrary API labels/fields, proactive stale-Save prevention, a static rollback snapshot, a pending overlay and ordinary undocumented editor Escape/Tab behavior through the written checks. Render:27, Constraints:27-29, Functional prompt:11-21, app_context:12,18 and Polish prompt:29-30 explicitly admit these choices; none supplies grounds for a false fail. This is a source-level fairness check, not a claim that such an alternate app was launched. In particular, an app using another durable engine could be observationally equivalent, but that would violate the inherited stack requirement; it is an assurance limitation, not a conforming alternative.

Raw evidence checked (not another review): qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json and its executed drivers. Recomputed SHA256 values match RESULTS.functional_sha256 (8e309112e55b495ff94bcc420483dc844b865bdf93cd3008522829914c2f3a2d) and prompt_sha256 (6405c6c52916b9480837a98b228a26e5fa0465241a3003d6da71b5f2bab907d1). Driver hashes for current_flow.cjs, runtime_flow.cjs and run_workflow.cjs also match the raw manifest. run_workflow.cjs:34 selects current_flow for S24, so unused legacy S24 code was not mistaken for the executed probe. current_flow.cjs:25-40 creates valid unique sources, then sends all four invalid titles through update.operation; RESULTS facts S24.title_collision_refusal and S24.title_empty_rejected record refusals and unchanged records under that update-only scope. RESULTS S11.html_error_line records bad.html line 6; S12.timer_error_line records delayed-error.js line 2; S13.promise_error_line records rejected-promise.js line 2. RESULTS S16.console_duration records "Complete ? 3.8 ms". Other raw observations incidentally contain durations (e.g. S04 "Run cancelled ? 58.5 ms" and S09 timeout statuses), showing the golden offers them; no current duration criterion demands those observations. Golden success cannot refute a missing rubric branch. None of G1-G4's wrong-app witnesses was executed in this audit. No paid/configured judge, Oracle score, target-model result or judge completion-time inference is made.
findings.impact: Four plausible source-audited false-pass witnesses, not executed: (1) save/load run the text in a bounded server VM with no visible outputs before returning the original bytes; (2) New/Save creates blank or duplicate titles while update validation is complete; (3) only synchronous HTML errors receive the document-line offset, leaving HTML timer/rejection lines script-relative; (4) elapsed duration appears only for successful runs. Each preserves the observations currently demanded by all five dimensions. The detailed requirement and protocol citations are in evidence.
findings.fix: Add bounded save/load execution-boundary evidence or resolve that absolute assurance through approved profile policy; add invalid new-title creation cases; add asynchronous complete-HTML line fixtures; collect duration from existing error/Stop/timeout scenarios. Preserve independent outcome ownership and reuse existing setups. Keep inherited exact-stack/runtime assurance limits explicit and do not alter the canonical harness, budgets, policy, or browser-source ban.

findings.title: criteria_are_independent_and_noncontradictory
findings.evidence:
Authoritative frozen workbook inspected with openpyxl: rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx, Quality Checks row 29 (check 28), says 'No two criteria grade the same thing twice, subsume each other, or demand incompatible products.' Internal Quality Checks row 29 has the historical whole-flow annotation; it is interpretation, not an override. Frozen skill references/quality-checks.md:120-121 permits flow bundling, but current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:13 explicitly supersedes a blanket bundling exemption: 'Share their browser scenario while scoring distinct promises separately. Preserve valid observations rather than inheriting a sibling verdict.'

Scope: inspected all 73 criterion blocks (58 Functional, 7 Polish, 6 Visual, 2 gates), all five judge prompts, app_context, and all six public notes. The main current ownership boundaries are substantially improved: functional/prompt.md:98-113 forbids inherited verdicts and repeated scenarios; S02 provides lowercase and JS-created CSS controls (:143-149); S22 separates retained durable reads from continued writes (:363-369); S23 separates server refusal from dirty-editor behavior; visual/prompt.md:17-22 expressly reserves mobile clipping/operability to Polish and Functional theme changes to Functional. Error message, exact line and restored preview are separately scored. No incompatible-product pair was demonstrated. Static restored previews versus interactive currently successful previews are compatible under behaviour.md:11-15 and app_context.md:18; optional provisional display, native keyboard controls, and mobile drawers/stacking likewise conform.

Confirmed source-level defect: .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:183 makes cw_js_error_rollback require 'the JS failure restores B, not A or failed-partial-dom; an ordinary recovery Run works.' The same extra conjunct appears for cw_html_error_rollback at :204, cw_timer_error_rollback at :225 and cw_promise_error_rollback at :246. Corresponding public behavior distinguishes restoration of the already successful render (environment/instructions/behaviour.md:13,15) from later ability to run it again (:13; policy.md:5). The prior successful preview and exact failed/last-good render comparison already establish the positive control and direct restoration observation. A later new Run is a distinct operation, not evidence necessary to determine which render was restored. Combining those two useful promises in each binary row erases the observed restoration result if later execution is broken; the converse also loses all recovery credit when only rollback is broken. This is the same separation that S22 explicitly preserves for durable readbacks versus later writes (judge.toml:351,358; prompt.md:367-369). The general instruction to score rows independently cannot rescue two conjuncts inside one binary row.

The four implicated weights are 0.90, 0.50, 0.50 and 0.50: 2.40 out of the parsed Functional total of 32.70 (58 rows), representing 0.0440 of final shaped reward above the common floor. This quantifies affected scoring mass, not a measured model reward or the exact amount an eventual reweighting would restore.

Raw evidence was checked directly, without consulting other reviews. qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json matches the frozen Functional judge and prompt SHA256 values (8e309112e55b495ff94bcc420483dc844b865bdf93cd3008522829914c2f3a2d and 6405c6c52916b9480837a98b228a26e5fa0465241a3003d6da71b5f2bab907d1). Its facts.S10.js_error_rollback.evidence has last_good.body='latest-good-B', restored='latest-good-B', recovered=true. S11, S12 and S13 likewise record respectively restored='js-error-recovered', 'html-error-recovered', and 'timer-error-recovered', each with recovered=true. Thus the actual observations distinguish restoration from subsequent execution. The executed drivers/runtime_flow.cjs:95-104 implements the same conjunction at :104: failed.body===lastGood.body && !failed.body.includes(c.candidate) && recovered. drivers/run_workflow.cjs:5,38,50 routes S10-S13 to that driver. These golden observations show the complete app satisfies both promises; they do not refute the partial-implementation counterexample. No deficient-app browser run, configured judge result, Oracle grade or target-model score was produced by this review.
findings.impact: Plausible partial implementation, reasoned from the explicit binary descriptors and not claimed as an executed mutation: the error handler correctly replaces the failed iframe with its saved lastGood document and reports the error/line, but leaves the Run button disabled because the exception path fails to clear a running/busy flag. In S10, successful A and distinct B establish real controls; the four-line bad.js fixture restores exactly latest-good-B. The next ordinary js-error-recovered Run cannot start. cw_js_error_rollback must receive 0 despite directly proven correct rollback, solely because of the distinct later execution failure. The same implementation defect affects the HTML, timer and Promise exception paths. Conversely, an app can clear the preview after failure yet accept the recovery Run; its recovery promise also has no independent credit in these four rows. A fully conforming alternative that restores a static snapshot (no live handlers) and then accepts Run is explicitly allowed and was not flagged; I also checked that a dead/no-op runner cannot earn these restoration outcomes from absence because the protocols require an actual prior successful DOM/log control. No separate credible duplicate-observable or incompatible-product witness was established.
findings.fix: Keep each existing S10-S13 browser scenario, successful controls and later recovery action, but assign restored-preview evidence and post-error successful-Run evidence to separate binary outcome owners; redistribute the existing criterion weight rather than adding duplicate setup or changing shared budgets/reward policy, and preserve one outcome when the other fails.

findings.title: negative_checks_have_positive_controls
findings.evidence:
Authority: inspected the actual frozen .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx with openpyxl, Quality Checks!row 31 (number 30): 'Any "rejects / hides / absent" check is paired with the matching success case, so a totally broken app can't earn it.' Internal Quality Checks!row 31 repeats this interpretation. Frozen harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/references/quality-checks.md:127-129 requires each rejects/hides/absent/unchanged leg to have the matching success case. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md:13 and :19 permit shared actual control facts while prohibiting inheritance of sibling verdicts; 'A dead feature must not earn credit for doing nothing.'

Confirmed source omission: .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:234 makes S09's control only a successful ordinary DOM/log run; :235-246 then supplies two infinite while loops, an infinite while loop inside a Promise callback, and an ordinary DOM/log recovery. There is no successful finite-loop execution control. The owned bar in tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:151-155 is 'Both top-level literal loops and the looping Promise callback terminate within the allowed budget margin with a time-limit reason, early logs preserved and successful recovery' (weight 2.75). Public environment/instructions/security.md:5 expressly requires 'ordinary source-written JavaScript: literal loops, functions, DOM changes, timers and Promise callbacks.' Thus a runner whose loop guard aborts at the first loop-body entry can obtain this substantial negative-result credit despite being unable to execute even a three-iteration literal loop. The generic control rule at functional/prompt.md:25 and :100 cannot supply an unperformed finite-loop control; none is specified in S09 or its explicit handoffs. This is a missing matching successful control, not a demand for a new unsupported feature or for a minimum five-second delay.

Concrete read-only local witness: executed an in-memory Node vm experiment using the exact three S09 sources. Before executing, a deliberately broken instrumenter inserted throw new Error('Execution stopped: five-second time limit') as the first statement of every while body, including replacement of the empty unbraced body. Native Promise callbacks were awaited normally. The braced fixture emitted before-braced-hang; the unbraced fixture emitted before-unbraced-hang; the Promise fixture emitted before-promise-hang and promise-loop-entered. Each produced the required time-limit reason and restored last-good-control. The ordinary timeout-recovered DOM/log source then completed. Conversely, let n=0; while (n<3) {n++;} document.body.innerHTML='finite-'+n;console.log('finite-'+n); immediately produced the time-limit reason with no finite result. This establishes the logical counterexample to the written bars; it is not a browser app mutation, configured judge run, or measured score. No task files were changed.

The corresponding scripted oracle also illustrates the absence of that discriminator, without proving a hosted false pass: qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/drivers/runtime_flow.cjs:89-94 establishes ordinary last-good, runs only those three infinite fixtures, and checks an upper duration bound, time-limit text, early markers, and recovery. It never runs a bounded while loop. The current golden's raw RESULTS.json facts.S09.literal_loop_deadline.evidence records real durations 5001.299, 5006.031 and 5002.286 ms and recovery=true; facts.S09.literal_loop_rollback records scope-recovered for all three restored bodies. These measurements support the golden's behavior, but a correct golden does not refute an incomplete discriminator.

Other negative checks inspected have meaningful controls. Functional prompt S01:119-121 saves a genuinely edited example and reads both the original and saved copy. S02:133-149 requires actual script/handler output, an enabled retained CSS button and successful ordinary click; its timer trial first observes the matching four-second timer complete. S03:156-161 observes completed-preview handlers before Stop and recovery afterward. S04:168-180 first executes the exact delayed callback/error uncancelled, then measures suppression relative to that baseline; B is positively completed before rollback checks. S05:188-198 executes own-document control, observes all four blocked outcomes and compares actual host values. S07:204-208 proves fetch and Image transport in a clean unprotected page, requires two separate visible refusal outcomes, compares deliveries, and requires ordinary recovery. S08:214-228 establishes a completed good render, tests each unsupported family separately and recovers; its supported-text outcome remains independent. S10-S13:253-300 use actual successful last-good renders, observed distinct failure triggers and recovery. S16:326-328 populates and observes console entries before Clear. S17:334-340 requires actual automatic execution plus successful manual execution of the same idle/queued source. S21-S24:354-389 establish successful saved records, current revisions and recovery before preserved-state/title/stale-refusal observations. S34:395 requires two actual theme changes with existing draft/output. S36:401-409 first completes short nested callbacks before timing out the longer nested variant. The two gates require authored Run output and an actual cross-context saved write/read (gates/render/judge.toml:23-27; gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-29). Polish and Visual assess positive rendered/reachable surfaces; focus specifically fails when no control can receive focus (polish/judge.toml:50).

Raw positive-control evidence independently inspected, rather than relying on product_pass flags: RESULTS.json facts.S02.css_inert_copy has script and handler counts 1 before and 1 after; S03.completed_stop has click/key/input counts 1 before and after, Run cancelled feedback and successful recovery; S04.supersede_pending has its uncancelled delayed/error counts 1, followed by unchanged counts after B; S17.autorun_debounce.evidence.first records auto-fired after 546.428 ms, and the off/queue cases observe 3000-ms windows with later manual outputs. S07 records expected text, image width 2 and baseline deliveries 2, then separate fetch/image refusal logs with deliveries still 2. S23 records actual same-identity revision progression 1->2->3 and 3->4->5 around the two stale refusals. S24 records successful current title write and QC Title Recovered revision 3 following refusal probes. The frozen functional judge and prompt SHA256 values exactly equal the raw run bindings (8e309112e55b495ff94bcc420483dc844b865bdf93cd3008522829914c2f3a2d and 6405c6c52916b9480837a98b228a26e5fa0465241a3003d6da71b5f2bab907d1); all actual_app_files hashes also match the frozen solution and inspected archived driver hashes match.

Conforming alternatives considered: a runtime may retain the last good picture while a candidate is pending, restore a static image, remove or disable controls after Stop, or implement CSS via an inert document copy; the explicit protocol controls permit these designs without forcing inaccessible controls. A finite-loop positive control should preserve those permissions and does not require a particular instrumentation technology or a minimum timeout delay. Full configured judge behavior, mutant app scores, hosted QC and Oracle/target-model scores remain unmeasured here. The review verdict concerns only check 30.
findings.impact: A otherwise functioning playground whose literal-loop instrumentation unconditionally throws a time-limit error on the first while-body entry. S09's two infinite top-level loops and infinite Promise-callback loop still emit their required early markers, show a time-limit reason, preserve the existing good render and allow ordinary recovery, meeting all written negative-result observations. A finite supported while loop such as let n=0; while(n<3){n++;} never produces n=3. This behavior was demonstrated in an in-memory Node vm witness; no browser mutant or paid judge was executed.
findings.fix: Before S09's negative fixtures, require actually successful bounded braced and unbraced literal loops and a bounded loop in a Promise callback to produce distinctive DOM/log results; reuse those observed facts for the corresponding termination outcomes while keeping rollback credit independent. Then test the immediate-abort loop mutant against the revised scenario.

findings.title: plural_asks_are_checked_across_all_matches
findings.evidence:
Scope and authority: reviewed only quality check 31. The actual frozen .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx was opened with openpyxl; Quality Checks!A32:D32 names check 31 and requires whole-collection coverage and unchanged guards that do not punish legitimate side-effects. Internal Quality Checks row 32 was read as interpretation only. The frozen skill's references/quality-checks.md:131-132 repeats that rule. qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md sections No hidden requirements, Independent credit takes precedence over flow grouping, and Runtime and model evidence govern this assessment. In the citations below, T means .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task/ and G means qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/.

Confirmed source defect: S05 uses a mutable, product-owned browser-tab title as an unconditional unchanged guard. T/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:189 says to record the playground page's own title before the authored probe. Lines 191-194 attempt four forbidden operations. Line 197 then requires: 'Fresh in-page reads of the playground's own title and storage show exactly their earlier values'. T/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:127 similarly requires 'actual host state is unchanged'. T/environment/instructions/security.md:3 prohibits snippet access to the parent document/storage, but neither that requirement nor the six public notes requires the application itself to keep its browser-tab title constant between Runs. T/environment/instructions/policy.md:5 permits the implementer to choose UI details. Thus the guard rejects a correctly sandboxed implementation that updates its own document.title with the completed run number, duration or run status. This is a legitimate side effect of pressing Run, and the false failure belongs directly to the second half of row 31. The storage probe uses a dedicated otherwise-unused key; no corresponding necessary false failure was established for that part.

Concrete read-only witness: considered a compliant implementation whose host increments a run counter on each successful Run and sets document.title to 'Playground - run N complete'. It uses an opaque sandbox, so the exact S05 source reports docRead=docWrite=storageRead=storageWrite='blocked', the cw-isolation-probe value remains null, and subsequent own-document execution works. The title legitimately advances from 'Playground - run 1 complete' to 'Playground - run 2 complete'. A Python evaluation of the source-prescribed before-title == after-title predicate returned False. This is an analytical predicate witness, not an executed alternative browser app or measured judge failure.

findings.title: criteria_are_outcome_based_and_browser_decidable
findings.evidence:
Authority: inspected the actual frozen XLSX using openpyxl, including Quality Checks row 33 (check 32), Internal Quality Checks row 33 and both full public check inventories. The row says, "Each criterion is a concrete, browser-observable outcome with durable evidence and distinctive probes. Reports every instance." Applied frozen SKILL.md and references/quality-checks.md section 32, staged-task-contract.md browser-only prompt/MCP rules, deterministic-checks.md prompt/schema/probe guidance, and qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md's tool-feasibility and actual-evidence corrections. Inspected all five judge/prompt pairs: 58 Functional, 7 Polish, 6 Visual and the two one-criterion gates, 73 criteria total. One bounded defect was found.

DURATION OBSERVABILITY GAP: frozen task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:274 describes cw_console_duration as "The completed Run shows a measured duration, not a blank or placeholder." Its only protocol is task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:326-328: Run console.log('history-first'); and observe "a measured run duration, not a placeholder", then perform another immediate DOM/log Run before theme/Clear observations. Neither this protocol nor another duration-owned assertion supplies an elapsed-time contrast, independently observed timing comparison, or required duration readback for a long-running control. Consequently, the visible evidence supports a numeric duration label, but cannot establish the claimed measurement. This is an actual requested behavior: task/environment/instructions/behaviour.md:19 says "Show how long each run took." The issue is bounded to this 0.20-weight Functional outcome, not the execution deadline outcomes.

RAW OBSERVATIONS: independently compared current frozen Functional judge/prompt SHA256 and all 22 recorded app-file hashes against golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json; all matched. facts['S16.console_duration'].evidence is only {"status":"Complete · 3.8 ms"}. The executed drivers/current_flow.cjs:7-11 runs the two immediate snippets and computes say('console_duration', /\d.*ms/.test(status), {status}); there is no duration calibration in that producer. A read-only local JavaScript evaluation of that exact predicate with a constant 'Complete · 3.8 ms' label returned true while no execution was measured. This confirms the raw predicate's weakness, not an actual configured-judge score for a mutated app. The golden itself does measure duration in solution/app/src/runtime.ts:79 (now() - started); that implementation fact cannot repair the browser-only criterion and is not asserted to be a golden defect.

OTHER OUTCOMES: no additional row-32 defect identified after reading all 73 descriptors and their complete protocols. Render requires authored distinctive DOM and console markers (gates/render/judge.toml:25), and Constraints requires a real new save plus exact independent-clean-context readbacks and reload (gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-27), without mandating JSON or inferring SQLite. Functional scenarios use executable distinct markers, exact entered error-line fixtures, completed renders, genuine negative controls, unchanged full records/revisions, dirty-field readbacks and observed request shapes. Representative raw observations substantiate that these are obtainable: S05 records all four 'blocked' values and unchanged title/storage; S07 records successful text/image controls then delivery count 2 before and after both refused authored probes; S22 records one actual restart with PID 16 -> 335, exact saved-record readbacks and a subsequent revision 2 -> 3 save; S23 records dirty fields and unchanged winner records in both editor orders; S36 observes outer callback entry, absent forbidden nested completion, time-limit feedback and last-good restoration. These facts were inspected directly, not accepted via the log's summary pass flags. Polish P02 gives a real keyboard route and control/focus observations; its responsive check permits tabs/drawers/scrolling. Visual criteria are rendered, anchored degree judgments, not hidden implementation claims.

CONFORMING ALTERNATIVES / TOOLS: a server-rendered library using opaque identities and a modal/composite control layout remains observable under the explicit observed-request and UI instructions. A runner that hides pending candidates behind the last-good render and disables stopped controls is expressly allowed, so I found no false-fail from requiring candidate visibility or forcing disabled controls. A correct duration display using rounded seconds is also not forbidden by the criterion; the suggested correction must not mandate the raw golden driver's milliseconds presentation. Source pins Playwright MCP 0.0.79 and supplies browser_run_code_unsafe recipes for clean contexts, real two-editor state and exact URL routing; the Functional dimension also exposes the single-use restart_app tool. The raw golden run uses direct pinned Playwright for browser actions and actual verifier MCP for restart. It does not establish configured browser-MCP/LLM judge completion, target-model scores, or hosted Oracle results. No new Docker/provider/browser run or task mutation was performed.
findings.impact: Plausible false-pass witness: keep the runner, saving and every other behavior correct, but replace the duration UI value with a constant 3.8 milliseconds (for example, display 'Complete · 3.8 ms' after every successful run without recording start/end time). Both S16 sources execute immediately, producing all requested history and DOM evidence, and the fixed plausible duration is observationally indistinguishable from a legitimate quick-run value under the written S16 protocol. The executed raw producer's exact duration predicate returns true for this constant label. For an independently timed multi-second callback the display would be demonstrably wrong, but no such duration comparison is required by cw_console_duration. The weak app was not run through the configured judge. Conforming alternatives challenged: rounded-second duration display, server-rendered records/opaque identity, and hidden pending preview with disabled post-Stop controls; no additional criterion false-fail was established.
findings.fix: Give cw_console_duration one broad browser-observed timing contrast: reuse an already successful delayed-callback control and a quick Run, record the displayed durations and elapsed start-to-completion times, and require compatible scale while allowing normal overhead, units and rounding; then exercise a constant-duration variant.

findings.title: cross_file_runtime_contract_is_consistent
findings.evidence:
Scope: actual frozen XLSX opened with openpyxl; Quality Checks row 50 (#49) says every repeated runtime fact agrees everywhere, and matching quality-checks.md:196-198 requires re-deriving the staged cross-file table. Both authoritative sheets were read, including Deterministic Checks rows 7, 8, 29, 31, 32, 33 and 36. Current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md was applied. All task-relative citations below are under .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task/.

CONFIRMED SOURCE CONFLICT 1, inherited restart semantics: environment/instructions/integration.md:7 requires saved records to survive a 'complete process restart over the same database'; tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:23 and :364 require the one completed process restart, and tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:351/:358 grade survival and subsequent writing from it. tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:16-19 promises to 'Stop the running application server process and relaunch the same application on the same database'; :47 reports 'restart complete: the server was relaunched'. In contrast, the generated helper in tests/test.sh:152-159 sends TERM, waits 50 x 0.1 seconds, then continues whether the old process group is still alive or not. Lines 160-169 launch and record a replacement PID without checking it remains alive; :171-183 accept any answering HTTP process. There is no required old-group termination check, escalation after the bounded wait, or new-PID liveness check. Therefore the helper's completed-restart claim can be false while the scored browser checks see unchanged state in the original process. This is an inherited shared-template conflict, not task-specific drift: task tests/test.sh is byte-identical to rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/test.sh, SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa; restart_mcp.py is also byte-identical, SHA256 03c1426f00e451f4d86b7547761715328c63cdf299f5f812f46c9fa3b44979b5. The frozen template's tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:80-84 makes the same stronger termination/relaunch claim.

CONFIRMED SOURCE CONFLICT 2, inherited undisclosed file-layout restriction: instruction.md:9 asks for the finished app/source/built frontend in /app; environment/instructions/integration.md:5 says start node /app/server.js and serve /app/public/index.html, with all startup assets inside /app (:9/:11). Neither the brief nor any of its six notes disallows symlinks to other files inside /app. tests/test.sh:72-83 nevertheless rejects every symlink except a path under /app/node_modules whose resolved target is also under /app/node_modules. The case at :81 ('*) exit 0 ;;') rejects even /app/public/index.html -> /app/dist/index.html, although both files remain inside the declared deliverable and the requested public path resolves normally. Because write_zero_reward ran at :60 and no suite is reached, a conforming app can receive zero without browser grading. This restriction is also byte-identical to the frozen template, not introduced by this candidate. A source-level branch trace establishes the rejection; no symlink fixture or Docker execution was performed in this scoped review.

CONSISTENT RE-DERIVED FACTS: port/listen 0.0.0.0:3000 and GET /api/health appear in integration.md:5, tests/test.sh:48/:108/:136/:164, tests/app_context.md:4, all five prompt opening URLs, and solution/app/server.js:12/:113. Entry /app/server.js is named in integration.md:5, checked/launched by test.sh:68/:97/:111, and installed by solution/solve.sh:4-7/:26. DB_PATH and default /app/app.db agree in integration.md:7, test.sh:98-109/:165/:187-189 and solution/app/server.js:8; the copy fallback substitutes its entry and database consistently. solve.sh:14-25 deletes only installation-time default database files after checking open descriptors, while server.js:118-127 uses CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS on process startup. Seed path /assets/seed_data.json matches instruction.md:5, integration.md:9, environment/Dockerfile:15 and task.toml:2; the seed contains no snippets and the public notes explicitly permit the app's own examples and preexisting saved library, so neither a nonempty later library nor absent runtime /assets is a drift. No fixed calendar timestamp or account fixture is promised: instruction.md:1, overview.md:7, policy.md:3 and app_context.md:8 all specify no sign-in. Dynamic updated_at values are not a fixed-clock violation.

The five-second snippet budget agrees between behaviour.md:9, security.md:5, app_context.md:18, Functional S09/S36 and runtime.ts:46-48/:95-118/:171; the 4.9-second instrumentation guard and 5.1-second watchdog are near-boundary implementation margins, not a different advertised deadline. The configured browser allowance up to about eight seconds is explicitly scheduling tolerance, not a new public execution budget. Later completed-preview interaction, static rollback, CSS copying and source line literals agree across behaviour.md:5-15, app_context.md:18, functional prompt S02-S13/S36 and their outcome descriptors. Source and shipped bundle agree at the inspected runtime/API sites (public/assets/index-VduTT3aN.js:28631/:28775/:28868/:28909/:29034/:29066/:29197); static/runner.html and public/runner.html are byte-identical. The .js/.html/.css dispatch, title case/trim, revision fields and frontend/server API routes agree in app.tsx, runtime.ts and server.js; the rubric permits discovered alternative routes and schemas. A server-rendered record response and off-origin app CDN assets are explicitly accepted by the prompts, consistent with the public brief.

Judging/scoring: task.toml:31-35 holds claude-code + z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx with the expected provider templates; all five judge fallbacks are claude-code, with no conflicting model. tests/Dockerfile:16-21 and environment/Dockerfile:9-11 agree on Express 5.1.0 and better-sqlite3 12.4.1, matching solution/app/package.json; Node is 22 in both images. The Codex compatibility configuration does not select the active judge. tests/scoring.toml:1-11 is canonical render/constraints gates 0, functional/polish/visual 0.6/0.2/0.2, floor 0.05; tests/tools/score.py:10/:28-48 reads that exact path/policy. tests/test.sh:193 exports APP_RESTART_HELPER and functional/judge.toml:18 passes literal $APP_RESTART_HELPER to the matching script/tool. Source counts are render 1, constraints 1, functional 58, polish 7, visual 6, with within-dimension weight sums 1/1/32.7/4/6. No stale quoted criterion count exists in task.toml; Functional prompt:9 correctly quotes 23 protocols, and all 23 headings occur once in its six-phase plan. Its quoted 9000-second budget (:113) equals functional/judge.toml:4. Gate timeouts 600+600 fit 1500; scored 9000+900+900 fit 11100; suite totals 12600 fit task verifier 13200. Those numeric agreements do not measure judge completion.

RAW OBSERVATION LIMITS: qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json was inspected directly, and every actual_app_files hash plus functional_sha256/prompt_sha256 matches the frozen task. Its restart object records one normal call, PID 16 -> 335, 5.645670579979196 seconds, isError=false. Its raw S22 data preserves Primary id 3 revision 2 and Second id 4 revision 1, followed by Primary revision 3 with unrelated records unchanged. The executed drivers/launch_workflow.py:59-71 extract this exact canonical helper and additionally wait for the original normal server to exit. S09 raw loop times are approximately 5001/5006/5002 ms; S36 shows nested-control-done retained, late-callback-entered then a time-limit reason, no forbidden nested completion, and recovery. These normal golden observations confirm the routine values but do not test a TERM-resistant app or the symlink rejection. The report explicitly uses direct Playwright, paid_provider=false and oracle_score_claimed=false; its 98.03-second scripted duration is not full configured LLM judge duration, Oracle reward, target-model score or portal evidence. No other reviewer findings were read, no task source was edited, and no new Docker/provider run was performed.
findings.impact: False pass (source-traced, not newly executed): a one-process Express app uses an in-memory snippet store, exposes the required UI/health and revisions, and installs process.on('SIGTERM', () => {}) while keeping its listener alive. The canonical helper waits about five seconds, launches a replacement that exits on EADDRINUSE, records its PID, and observes HTTP from the original app. It returns success and restart_mcp.py announces a completed restart. All S22 readbacks and a later write can succeed in the original memory store even though actual process replacement would lose the data. False fail (source-traced, not newly executed): an otherwise fully conforming Express/SQLite app ships /app/public/index.html as a symlink to /app/dist/index.html, with all compiled assets inside /app. The public path serves normally, but tests/test.sh:72-83 exits before launch because the link is outside /app/node_modules, retaining reward zero. Ordinary no-symlink golden success does not refute either witness.
findings.fix: Resolve these upstream shared-template conflicts without silently editing this task's canonical harness: require bounded old-process-group termination and verified replacement-PID liveness before restart success, and either publicly document the exact symlink policy or provide an approved canonical rule accepting safe in-/app links. Bind new targeted resistant-process and conforming-symlink evidence plus the normal golden flow to the approved replacement candidate.
